name: Liscannor

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Liscannor is an Irish mythological site close to the Cliffs of Moher. The small town holds a holy well that the source ties to Brigit, the goddess turned saint. On February 1 the faithful gather there, on Brigit feast day and the Celtic feast of Imbolc or spring awakening. A path of round trips runs up and down a hillside before a person visits the well itself. The waters of the well trickle down a rocky wall. That wall reaches within the hill. This setting leads scholars to think the well once sheltered a goddess rather than a saint.

okr.objective: State the natural and sacred place of Liscannor as the source tells it.
